discovery: Electron quantum optics: on-demand coherent single-electron sources in quantum conductors

nominees.name: Gwendal Fève
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

nominees.name: Bernard Plaçais
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire de Physique de l'École Normale Supérieure, Paris, France

subfield: Condensed matter physics / mesoscopic quantum transport
motivation: The nominees turned single electrons in solid-state conductors into controllable quantum particles, founding the field of electron quantum optics. Fève, Plaçais and co-workers realized the first on-demand coherent single-electron source (mesoscopic capacitor, Science 2007), emitting individual electrons and holes into quantum Hall edge channels with high precision. Glattli and co-workers realized levitons (Nature 2013): minimal-excitation Lorentzian voltage pulses that inject clean single electrons without accompanying electron-hole pairs, as predicted by Levitov. With electronic Hong-Ou-Mandel and Hanbury Brown-Twiss experiments, current-noise tomography of single-electron wavefunctions, and the direct observation of anyonic braiding statistics in a fractional quantum Hall collider (Science 2020), these works established that quantum-optical concepts carry over to fermions in conductors, where interactions and the Fermi sea fundamentally change the physics. They provide the experimental basis for flying-electron qubits, quantum current standards, and studies of quantum fluctuations and thermodynamics at the single-particle level.
